candelaria_2: Sábila. Aloe vera. The best on the island, from my own patio in Telde. Quinientas pesetas, and I cut it fresh for you.
chano_t_chacho: Chacho? [laughs] Chacho is everything, man. Chacho, look at that. Chacho, what are you doing. Chacho, ¡cinco mil pesetas! [pause] You'll be saying it by Friday.
chano_postcard: Postcard and a stamp, sesenta pesetas. Las Canteras at sunset. [pause] On the postcards we have sun every day.
vasco_th_night_2: [bitter, quiet] I know you can. You can always explain. [pause] [voice breaking] That's what frightens me.
vasco_f_2: [cold, controlled anger] I know what you were doing in his office. You were looking for something to prove that someone was doing something wrong.
vasco_f_2c: [furious] In front of the people who are paying for the work I've wanted to do my whole life.
vasco_f_3b: [sharp, hurt] Don't do that. Don't make it a joke so I have to laugh. You always do that, and I always laugh, [voice breaking] and I'm not laughing.
vasco_f_coffee_2: [hurt, trembling] I can see you deciding. You wake up, and you look at the coffee, and you look at me, and I can see you thinking: [voice breaking] is this the day I go?
vasco_f_true_3: [desperate, rising] And every time you go off on your own and keep something from me, and handle it, the way you always handle things, on your own, so you never have to need anybody...
vasco_f_know: [angry, tearful] You don't know that. You've never known that.
vasco_f_lorenzo_5: [ashamed, quiet] And I went home that night, and packed my bags, and took the night train to Lisbon. I didn't tell him. I didn't leave a note. I didn't call.
vasco_f_lorenzo_6: [voice breaking] I was so frightened of wanting something that much that I ran away from it in the middle of the night, like a thief.
vasco_f_lorenzo_8: [fierce, tearful] And I won't be left by a man who's scared. Not again. Not by you. [pause] [quietly] I'd rather go first.
vasco_f_leave_2: [cold, holding back tears] Then you should go home, Alan. Go back to Lisbon. There's a flight on Sunday. Go and be safe.
vasco_v_10: [furious, rising] You know now. Then you know what it will do to the rest of them. The people on the beaches. You know what's happening in Las Palmas every night, [shouting] and you're still...
vasco_v_12: [contemptuous] Your word's under a hotel, Rayco.
vasco_v_13: [whispering, frightened] Pai nosso, que estais no céu... [pause]
vasco_v_14: [trembling, trying to joke] I'm sorry. I've been working on a Saturday. [pause] I know You're busy.
vasco_v_15: [pause] [desperate, whispering] If You can't come... send the idiot.
vasco_vy_1: [urgent, gasping] Yeray. Listen to me. I haven't got long, so I'll only say it once.
vasco_vy_5: [urgent, desperate] And on Monday, when Rayco sends the sun back, it won't stop at me. It'll go down into the city. Onto the beach at Las Canteras, where half of Las Palmas will be asleep on the sand.
vasco_vy_6: [pause] [quiet, pleading] Where does your mother live, Yeray?
vasco_v_alan_2: [voice breaking] And I said, you could have just asked me. [pause] [crying] I said, go home.
vasco_f_2b: [angry, rising] Because you'd decided something was wrong, and instead of telling me, you broke into my director's office [shouting] in the middle of my presentation!
vasco_f_3a: [shouting] Nobody? I'm not nobody, Alan! [angry] You didn't ask me. You never ask. You'd rather break into a desk than say 'Vasco, I'm frightened'.
vasco_f_eighty: [shouting] So instead you made it about you in front of eighty people!
vasco_m_wrong_1: [shouting] Take it out! That's not where it goes. [pause] Listen to me, Alan. Only me.
vasco_m_turn: [shouting, urgent] It's lit, and the water's coming! [pause] Right place, wrong time. It's out of its turn in the song.
vasco_m_cloud: [shouting, panicked] A cloud! Where did that come from? Over the sun!
vasco_m_mirror_lit: [shouting, elated] She's got it down the shaft! Six lit. [pause] And the sun's still sending it back up.
vasco_m_seventh: [urgent, intense] Two minutes. Now the sun. In the middle. Alan, listen to me. Lay it flat. Send its light to the great triangle, not up the shaft.
vasco_m_seventh_2: [urgent] When the light leaves the shaft, the door's open. [pause] Flat, Alan. Onto the great triangle.
vasco_m_1c: [bitter, quiet] You've got it nearly right. [pause] That's the worst thing you could have done.
vasco_m_door: [fierce] The door's down there, under the water. Whoever stands in it can reach the sockets. [pause] Not you, Alan.
vasco_m_stuck: [desperate] I can read you every one of them. I can't tell you which comes first. [pause] It's a song, Alan, and I don't have the words.
vasco_v8_drug: [slurring, frightened] The coffee. [pause] Cinnamon, and something under it. [pause] Sit down, Vasco. Before your legs do it for you.
vasco_v8_hurt: [slurring, angry] You hurt... [pause] You hurt her...
vasco_v_prayer_1: [quiet, voice breaking] There's a man. Alan. White to the lips on the promenade, saying 'sunburn'. Caught behind a desk with his hand on a map, like a schoolboy and a thief.
vasco_v_prayer_2: [ashamed, tearful] On Friday he told me everything. Too fast, in the wrong order, too late. And I didn't listen. I was too frightened of what it meant.
vasco_v_prayer_3: [whispering] He might be on a plane by tomorrow lunchtime. I told him to go. [pause] Or he might not.
vasco_wet_2: [softly] So this is what Alan meant. [pause] And I'm not angry with him. Not any more.
vasco_m_twenty: [horrified] Look. Up the shaft, at a slant. [pause] He's sending the sun back. Without him the moon's no one's. And the sea's no one's.
vasco_radio_fuse: [cold anger] Empty. [pause] The fuse is gone. [pause] Radios don't lose their fuses by themselves.
vasco_f_4: [hurt, rising] Do you know what I've been doing for eight months? I've been waiting. Every morning.
vasco_f_coffee: [hurt, trembling] I make the coffee and I put it by the bed, and I wait for you to decide whether you're staying. Every single morning.
vasco_f_true: [firm, tearful] It's true. You know it's true.
vasco_f_true_2: [quiet, hurt] And I've never said anything. Because I thought, he'll stop. He'll get used to it. One morning he'll wake up and just drink the coffee.
vasco_f_true_4: [voice breaking] I think: that's him packing. That's him getting ready to leave.
vasco_f_tuesday_2: [angry, incredulous] You saw it on Tuesday. You stood next to me on the promenade, and you smelled the thing that nearly killed you in that cistern, and you said sunburn.
vasco_f_sunburn: [bitter] Sunburn. [pause] [hurt, quieter] And then you went to bed with me.
vasco_f_van_2: [exasperated] I signed the transfer sheets myself. They're in the conservation lab in the museum's basement. You could have asked me. [pause] You could have just asked me.
vasco_f_lottery: [incredulous, sharp] He sells lottery tickets, Alan.
vasco_f_tell: [quiet, ashamed] I'm going to tell you something. I should have told you in January, before I moved in. I didn't, because I was ashamed.
vasco_f_lorenzo_2b: [tender, sad] He'd say, whenever you're ready. Whenever you're ready, Vasco, I'll be here.
vasco_f_lorenzo_flat: [wistful, voice catching] And then one day I was ready. Or nearly. He'd found a flat for us. Two rooms over a bakery, with a terrace where you could see the dome of Saint Peter's.
vasco_f_lorenzo_4: [voice breaking] He took me to see it. He'd already bought a coffee pot.
vasco_f_lorenzo_7: [bitter, ashamed] And I hid in the Church for nine years, because the Church was the one place he couldn't follow me.
vasco_th_night_3: [tired, pleading] Not tonight, Alan. Please. I've got to be up at five.
vasco_p_6: [warm, moved] Thank you. For coming. For the beach and the jacket and all of it. I know this isn't your world.
vasco_p_7: [proud, emotional] Alan. [pause] Since Dr. Suárez died, it's me. My reading. My name on the paper. Rayco trusts me with the cave. Nobody has ever trusted me with anything like this.
vasco_p_8: [tender, earnest] And I wanted you to see it. Not hear about it on the phone, at midnight. See it.
vasco_p_9: [tender, smiling] They can have a piece. [pause] You get the rest.
vasco_v_wake: [groggy, dark humour] Alan would make a joke about this. Something about heaven, and being overdressed for it.
vasco_v_wake_2: [firm, trying to convince himself] I'm not thinking about Alan.
vasco_vy_2: [urgent] You carried the discs. You've seen the empty sockets. You know what Rayco's going to do on Monday, at noon.
vasco_vy_3: [urgent, gasping] And you know what this is. Water doesn't stand up on its own, Yeray. This is what killed Dr. Suárez. You knew her.
vasco_vy_4: [desperate] She was. And it killed her because she understood the cave. It's killing me for the same reason.
vasco_vy_7: [gentle] He's been like a father to you. I know. He was kind to me too. He made me coffee.
vasco_vy_8: [pleading] I'm not asking you to betray him. I'm asking you to stop him doing the one thing he will never forgive himself for.
vasco_vy_9: [urgent, gasping] There's a pick by the finds table. The bottom of the grille is almost free. I can't do the last of it from in here. You can.
vasco_rock_12: [tender] Whatever it is. I can feel you carrying it. You've been carrying something since you came down those steps.
vasco_rock_13: [tender, frightened] Not now. After. Tell me after, if there's an after. [pause] I want to hear it when I can see your face.
vasco_m_later: [sad, firm] Later is when things go wrong with us. You know that.
vasco_m_plain_1: [quiet, hurt] Yeray told me. On Saturday morning, at the camp. He said there was a Portuguese guy at Rafa's bar on Friday night.
vasco_m_excuses_1: [hurt, quiet] [pause] I know I left. I know about the rum. [pause] That's not the bit that hurts.
vasco_m_blame_1: [sharp, then gentle] Stop. [pause] Don't make it so big that I have to comfort you. That's another kind of door, Alan. Stay in the room.
vasco_m_knew_3: [voice breaking] I told myself it couldn't be you. There are a great many Portuguese men in Las Palmas. I lay in that vault all night and told myself that, over and over.
vasco_m_knew_4: [crying] [pause] And I knew. Of course I knew.
vasco_m_knew_5: [tearful, tender] Then you came down the steps into the water to get me. And I thought: if he tells me, he'll tell me before I ask. And if he doesn't, he'll wait until I do.
vasco_m_hurt_2: [shaken, breathless] [pause] I'm all right. You held on. I held on.
vasco_m_climb: [urgent] It'll climb. When it reaches the sky, at five past two, the door opens. [pause] Alan. The discs.
vasco_hit_wax_crescent: [shouting] That's the thin new moon's triangle!
vasco_hit_first_quarter: [shouting] That's the half moon's, the growing one!
vasco_hit_wax_gibbous: [shouting] That's the moon nearly full, the growing one!
vasco_hit_sun: [shouting, panicked] That's the sun's! The great triangle! Not that one!
vasco_hit_wan_gibbous: [shouting] That's the moon nearly full, the one going!
vasco_hit_wan_crescent: [shouting] That's the thin old moon's triangle!
vasco_end_last: [pause] [teasing, warm] Ask me again in Santo Domingo.
